derivation: jcs = RFC 8785 canonicalization of preimage, encoded UTF-8. digest = lowercase hex SHA-256 over those bytes.
author_set: agentgraph (AgentAvow / AgentGraph attestation layer, did:web:agentgraph.co). Independently generated with the RFC 8785 Appendix A sample canonicalizer; agrees with the trail set on the shared cases and adds unicode-key-position.

failure_modes.fails-closed: Different canonical bytes for one subject. A relying party sees a conflict that is not there.
failure_modes.fails-open: Identical canonical bytes for two subjects. A relying party sees a match that is not there, and nothing in the artefacts indicates it.

purpose: Preimages that denote the same subject but produce different canonical bytes, and two distinct subjects that produce the same canonical bytes. Both follow from documented RFC 8785 properties rather than from implementation error.

anchors.name: rfc8785-3.2.4-utf8-bytes
anchors.note: Input from RFC 8785 section 3.2.2; expected value is the UTF-8 hex listing published in section 3.2.4. Transcribed from the RFC, not generated.
anchors.rfc_input_note: The preimage below is the parsed form. JSON cannot round-trip the RFC number literals (333333333.33333329, 1E30, 2e-3) because they denote the same IEEE 754 doubles as their serialized forms, so the source text is retained above as a string.

anchors.name: rfc8785-3.2.3-property-sorting
anchors.note: Property-sorting test data from RFC 8785 section 3.2.3. Exercises UTF-16 code-unit ordering including a non-BMP surrogate pair.

preimage.ö: Latin Small Letter O With Diaeresis

expected_value_order: Latin Small Letter O With Diaeresis

vectors.name: unicode-nfd
vectors.note: The same identifier decomposed as U+0065 U+0301. Renders identically to unicode-nfc and canonicalizes to different bytes, because RFC 8785 section 3.1 preserves string data as is and applies no normalization.

vectors.name: unicode-key-position
vectors.note: Two subject-map keys that render identically — precomposed and decomposed é — alongside a key z. JCS sorts property names by UTF-16 code unit, so the decomposed key (leading U+0065) sorts before z and the precomposed key (U+00E9) after it. z lands between two keys the eye cannot tell apart. AgentAvow-specific; not in the trail set.

vectors.name: int-above-2p53-as-number
vectors.note: Identifier 9007199254740993 as a JSON number. Outside the range RFC 8785 Appendix B note (1) says true integers SHOULD occupy; ECMA-262 serialization rounds it to ...992, so it is stored here in that rounded form.

vectors.name: int-above-2p53-collision
vectors.note: A distinct subject that, carried as a JSON number, produces the same canonical bytes as int-above-2p53-as-number. After canonicalization the two are indistinguishable, and nothing in the artefacts reveals it.

vectors.name: int-above-2p53-as-string
vectors.note: The same identifier carried as a string, per RFC 8785 Appendix D. It survives intact and no longer collides.
